title: Normalized completed-to-native coefficient inclusion
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-embedding $i:E\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Fix a NativeGeometry for $\ell$ [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-compact-support-data]. There is a Change from the completed integral coefficient system for $E$ to the native locally finite coefficient system, commuting with inverse image along every scheme morphism [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. For every scheme $T$ and every normalized CoefficientPresentation $C$ of $E$ on $T$ with embedding $i$ [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-realization-data], its map at $T$ is exactly $C.integralMap$: inverse completion identification, normalized integral-to-rational inclusion, then normalized inclusion into the native function sheaf. This statement constructs coefficient maps only; it constructs no compact-support natural transformation.

proof.text: Use continuous finite-quotient realization to identify the completed integral ring sheaf with continuous $\mathcal O_E$-valued functions. Define its map to the native ring by composing these functions with $\mathcal O_E\to E\xrightarrow{i}\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The extension norm makes $i$ continuous; the image lies in the finite-dimensional field $i(E)$, so it satisfies the native local-finiteness condition. Pointwise addition, multiplication and one make this a ring-sheaf map.

proof.text: For a scheme morphism, both composites on the direct-image side precompose a function with the same base-change projection and postcompose with the same coefficient embedding. The pointwise NativeGeometry.pull normalization identifies the native map. Take inverse-image adjoints to obtain the Change.square identity.

proof.text: For any normalized CoefficientPresentation, its finite-constant and residue equations determine the completion identification: compose with each finite quotient projection, where both maps coincide. Limit uniqueness makes the integral maps equal. The integralInclusion_normalized and rationalInclusion_normalized equations then identify the composite with the same pointwise function map. Extensionality proves the asserted equality for every presentation.

theorem native_completed_coefficient_change [G : NativeGeometry.{u} l]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (i : E →ₐ[Padic l] PadicAlgCl l) :
    ∃ a : PurCompactSupport.Change (PurCompactSupport.completed l E) (nativeCoefficients l),
      ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (C : CoefficientPresentation l T E i),
        a.map T = C.integralMap l T
